# Reiver documentation

> Reiver is an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, prompt-management system, and OpenTelemetry observability platform with MCP-based management.

## Start here

- Choose a track: https://docs.reiver.ai/quickstart
- Flow + Prompt Hub: https://docs.reiver.ai/flow/getting-started
- Watch: https://docs.reiver.ai/watch/
- Complete Reiver: https://docs.reiver.ai/quickstart
- Complete machine-readable guide: https://docs.reiver.ai/llms-full.txt
- Shared Session and Identity Contract: https://docs.reiver.ai/flow/session-telemetry
- MCP setup: https://docs.reiver.ai/agent/mcp-setup
- MCP resources: connect to https://reiver.ai/mcp and read agent://onboarding

## Credential contract

- Provider keys stay in Reiver.
- One SDK key value is bound separately as REIVER_FLOW_API_KEY and REIVER_WATCH_API_KEY in the application runtime.
- REIVER_AGENT_TOKEN is a separate scoped MCP credential and stays in the coding-agent environment.

## Agent onboarding contract

- Honour the selected track. Flow and Watch are independently completable; do not require evidence from the unselected product.
- Infer and confirm the application's users, purpose, business outcomes, Session and Identity Contract and important risks before creating labels or controls.
- Save the confirmed session unit, start/end events, 30-minute abandonment fallback, stable pseudonymous user ID, anonymous policy and tenant scoping in gateway_settings.agent_soul.
- There is no separate autonomy-mode selector. MCP token scopes are the hard technical boundary; the owner's assignment defines the agent's behavioural authority.
- Prove the selected track's baseline before adding prompts, labels, profiles, guardrails, dashboards or alerts.
- Within explicit write authority, act without repeated approval, verify every change through MCP and return evidence plus rollback paths.

Do not treat HTTP 200 alone as a completed Flow integration or one trace as completed Watch observability. Use the selected track's definition of done.
